1 رَمَثَ , (S, TA,) aor.
رَمُثَ , (TK,) inf. n. رَمْثٌ, (K,) He put a thing into a right, or proper, state, or adjusted it; and wiped it with his hand. (S, K, * TA.) He collected together a thing, and put it into a right, or proper, state, or adjusted it. (As, TA.) ＝
-A2- رَمِثَتِ الإِبِلُ, (T in art. طلح, S, M,) aor.
رَمَثَ , (TA,) inf. n. رَمَثٌ, (S, M, K,) The camels ate رِمْث alone, without any change of food: (T in art. طلح:) or had a complaint from eating رِمْث: (S, M, K:) AHn says that the complaint thus caused is a looseness, or flux of thin excrement from the bowels, consequent upon eating رمث when hungry; and that one fears for the camels in this case. (M.) ―
-b2- رَمِثَ أَمْرُهُمْ, aor.
رَمَثَ , (K,) inf. n. رَمَثٌ, (TA,) (assumed tropical:) Their affair, or case, or state of things, became confused. (K.) ＝
-A3- رَمِثَ, aor.
رَمَثَ ; and رَمَثَ, aor.
رَمُثَ ; inf. n. of each رَمَثٌ; He stole. (T.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
